config.title: Build object diff utility

intro.title: Build object diff utility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a utility function that compares two JavaScript objects and returns the differences between them. You will learn how to use loops and conditional statements to iterate through object properties and identify changes. The main technologies involved are JavaScript objects, the `for...in` loop, and comparison operators. This exercise will help you understand how to work with dynamic data structures and create reusable code for data comparison tasks.
intro.usecase: Object diff utilities are essential in modern web applications for tracking changes in data structures. They're commonly used in form validation systems to detect which fields users have modified before submitting updates. In collaborative tools like Google Docs or Figma, diffs help synchronize changes between multiple users by identifying exactly what properties changed. Version control systems like Git use similar algorithms under the hood to compare file changes between commits. Developers also implement object diffs in state management libraries like Redux to optimize re-renders by determining which components need updates.

objectives: Implement a function that compares two objects and identifies differences
Construct a recursive algorithm to handle nested object structures
Manipulate object properties to extract changed values between versions
Apply type checking to handle different data types during comparison
Initialize a result object to store identified differences systematically
Configure comparison logic to handle both added and removed properties
Integrate the diff utility into a test scenario to validate functionality

steps.title: Create the diff function signature
steps.instruction: Create a function called diff that takes two parameters: obj1 and obj2. The function should return an empty object for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to include both parameters and return an empty object {}.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named diff is created with two parameters and returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The diff function exists with parameters obj1 and obj2, and returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the diff function signature correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named diff, takes two parameters (obj1 and obj2), and returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function signature isn't quite right. Create a function called diff that accepts obj1 and obj2 as parameters and returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize an empty result object
steps.instruction: Inside your diff function, create an empty object called 'result' to store the differences.
steps.hint: You can create an empty object using curly braces {}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The diff function now has an empty result object ready to store differences.
successCriteria: An empty object named 'result' is created inside the diff function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you create an empty object named 'result' inside the diff function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating an empty object called 'result' inside the diff function.

steps.title: Get all unique keys from both objects
steps.instruction: Inside your diff function, create a Set containing all keys from both oldObj and newObj using Object.keys() and the spread operator.
steps.hint: You can combine arrays of keys using the spread syntax: [...keys1, ...keys2] inside new Set().
steps.expectedOutcome: Your diff function will have a Set variable containing all unique keys from both input objects.
successCriteria: The diff function contains a Set created with Object.keys() and spread operator for both oldObj and newObj.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using Object.keys() on both objects and combining them with the spread operator inside new Set().
steps.feedbackWrong: create a Set containing all keys from both oldObj and newObj using Object.keys() and spread syntax.

steps.title: Iterate through all keys
steps.instruction: Add a for...of loop to iterate through the Set of all keys inside your diff function.
steps.hint: Use the syntax 'for (const key of allKeys) { }' where allKeys is the Set you created in the previous step.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your diff function will have a for...of loop that iterates through all unique keys from both objects.
successCriteria: The diff function contains a for...of loop that iterates through a Set of keys.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using a for...of loop to iterate through the Set of keys.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loop structure isn't quite right. Remember to use for...of to iterate through the Set of keys.

steps.title: Check if key exists in both objects
steps.instruction: Inside your for...of loop, add an if statement to check if the current key exists in both oldObj and newObj using hasOwnProperty.
steps.hint: Use the hasOwnProperty method on each object to test for the key's existence.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your diff function will now include a conditional check inside the loop to identify keys present in both input objects.
successCriteria: The for...of loop contains an if statement that uses hasOwnProperty to check if the key exists in both oldObj and newObj.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking both objects (oldObj and newObj) using hasOwnProperty inside the if condition.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on this step: inside the loop, add an if statement that checks if the key exists in both objects using hasOwnProperty.

steps.title: Handle keys that exist in both objects
steps.instruction: Inside the for...of loop, when a key exists in both objects, write an if statement to check if both values are objects. If they are, recursively call diff on those values; otherwise, compare the primitive values directly.
steps.hint: Use typeof to check if both oldObj[key] and newObj[key] are objects (and not null). If they are, assign the recursive diff result to result[key]. If not, compare the values and assign to result[key] only if they differ.
steps.expectedOutcome: The diff function now includes logic to deeply compare nested objects when a key exists in both input objects, using recursion for objects and direct comparison for primitives.
successCriteria: The for...of loop contains an if statement that checks if both values are objects (and not null) and recursively calls diff, otherwise compares primitive values and assigns to result only if they differ.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your if statement correctly checks that both values are objects (using typeof and null check) and handles the recursive call and primitive comparison separately.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logic for handling keys in both objects is missing or incorrect. Remember to check if both values are objects (and not null) for recursion, and compare primitives directly otherwise.

steps.title: Handle keys only in first object
steps.instruction: Inside the for...of loop, add an else if statement to check if the key exists only in oldObj. If true, add it to the result object with the value { old: oldObj[key], new: undefined }.
steps.hint: Use the hasOwnProperty method or the 'in' operator to check if a key exists in an object. The syntax would be: else if (oldObj.hasOwnProperty(key) && !newObj.hasOwnProperty(key)) { ... }
steps.expectedOutcome: The diff function will now correctly identify keys that are present in the old object but missing in the new object, adding them to the result with their old value and marking the new value as undefined.
successCriteria: An else if condition is added inside the loop to check if the key exists only in oldObj, and the result object is updated with { old: oldObj[key], new: undefined } for those keys.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the condition correctly checks if the key is in oldObj but not in newObj, and that you're adding the proper structure to the result object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't yet handle keys only in the first object. Review the hint and analogous example to add the missing logic.

steps.title: Handle keys only in second object
steps.instruction: Inside the for...of loop, add an else if condition to check if the current key exists only in the second object (newObj). If true, add that key to the result object with the value { old: undefined, new: newObj[key] }.
steps.hint: Use an else if statement after your existing condition. Check if the key is in newObj but not in oldObj using the in operator or hasOwnProperty.
steps.expectedOutcome: The diff function will now detect keys that are new in the second object and record them with undefined as the old value.
successCriteria: The else if condition correctly identifies keys only in newObj and adds them to result with the specified structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your condition correctly checks if the key is in newObj but not in oldObj, and assigns the value as { old: undefined, new: newObj[key] }.
steps.feedbackWrong: The condition for handling keys only in the second object is missing or incorrect. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Filter out unchanged values
steps.instruction: After the for...of loop, add code to filter out entries from the result object where the old and new values are equal.
steps.hint: You can create a new object by iterating through the result's keys and only copying entries where the values differ.
steps.expectedOutcome: The diff function will now return a cleaned result object that only contains entries where values actually changed.
successCriteria: Code after the loop filters the result object to remove entries where old and new values are equal.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're actually filtering the result object after the loop completes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The filtering step is missing or incorrect. After the loop, you need to remove entries from result where values didn't change.

steps.title: Return the result object
steps.instruction: Return the result object from the diff function.
steps.hint: At the end of your function, use the return keyword followed by the variable name that holds your result object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The diff function will now return the computed differences between the two objects.
successCriteria: The diff function returns the result object using the return keyword.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the return keyword with the correct variable name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't return the result object. Add a return statement at the end.
